english: Let $p:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by $p(x)=(1+x)(1+2x)(1+3x)(1+4x)(1+5x)(1+6x)$. Then the value of $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0}\dfrac{p(x)-1-21x}{x^{2}}$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $p:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $p(x)=(1+x)(1+2x)(1+3x)(1+4x)(1+5x)(1+6x)$ द्वारा परिभाषित है। तब $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0}\dfrac{p(x)-1-21x}{x^{2}}$ का मान ______ है।
solution_full: At $x=0$: $p(0)=1$, so the numerator tends to $0$, as does $x^{2}$.
Logarithmic derivative: $\dfrac{p'(x)}{p(x)}=\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{6}\dfrac{k}{1+kx}$, so $p'(0)=1+2+\dots+6=21$. Hence the derivative of the numerator, $p'(x)-21$, also tends to $0$.

By L'Hospital's rule twice (both stages are $\dfrac00$ forms of differentiable functions): $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0}\dfrac{p(x)-1-21x}{x^{2}}=\lim_{x\to0}\dfrac{p'(x)-21}{2x}=\lim_{x\to0}\dfrac{p''(x)}{2}=\dfrac{p''(0)}{2}$.
Therefore the limit is $\dfrac{350}{2}=175$. (This is the coefficient of $x^{2}$ in $p(x)$, the sum of the products $jk$ over $1\le j<k\le6$.)
originality_note: New: a second-order L'Hospital limit on a six-factor product, where the second derivative at 0 is obtained from (sum k)^2 - (sum k^2) (way 5). Closest known: lim ((1+x)(1+2x)(1+3x) - 1)/x (first order) and lim (1 - cos x cos 2x cos 3x)/x^2. Different because: the linear term is removed, so the second-order coefficient (an elementary symmetric sum) must be found.

concept_use.L'Hospital Rule: The limit is reduced by L'Hospital's rule twice to p''(0)/2, after checking both 0/0 stages.

key_step: Applying L'Hospital twice and getting p''(0) from the logarithmic derivative.
justification: A routine chain: two L'Hospital steps and a second derivative of a product evaluated at 0; no insight needed, numerical answer. Level with the routine limit anchor 2025-P2-Q1 (L2).
